 Zoho co-founder and Chief Scientist Sridhar Vembu has cited China’s 18% youth unemployment rate, arguing that India needs to rethink its traditional employment model. 
He believes the country must place greater emphasis on entrepreneurship and self-employment as Artificial Intelligence (AI) and automation increasingly put pressure on conventional salaried jobs.
Vembu made these remarks while resharing a post on social media platform X about rising youth unemployment in China.
According to China’s National Bureau of Statistics, the unemployment rate among people aged 16 to 24, excluding students, stood at around 18% in September 2026, down from 18.9% in August. Meanwhile, unemployment among people aged 25 to 29 reached 7.2% in August, continuing an upward trend that began in June.
 China Expects 12.7 Million University Graduates to Enter the Job Market
 Around 12.7 million university graduates are expected to enter China’s job market in 2026, marking the highest number on record. Notably, China is a global manufacturing hub and has a trade surplus of approximately USD 1.2 trillion. Despite this economic position, employment opportunities for young people remain a major challenge.
The reshared social media post attributed the situation to a slowdown in the property sector, job cuts at technology companies and the growing adoption of AI. It also claimed that some of China’s largest companies had privately warned the government that wider AI adoption could eliminate 30% or more of their jobs. However, these claims were made in the post and have not been independently verified.
 AI and Automation Increasing Pressure on Traditional Jobs
 According to Vembu, modern education systems and economic structures prepare young people primarily for jobs that offer a steady salary. However, opportunities for such jobs are no longer growing at the same pace. In addition, AI and automation are creating new challenges for traditional employment opportunities.
He argued that India should not rely solely on large corporations as the primary source of employment. Instead, the country needs to create an environment where young people can start their own businesses and achieve financial independence through self-employment.
 Greater Focus on Entrepreneurship and Self-Employment Needed: Sridhar Vembu
 Sharing his views on X, Vembu wrote, "What is the solution? Dramatic gains in entrepreneurship and self-employment. Policymakers must pay heed." 
His remarks come at a time when the changing nature of employment, driven by AI and automation, is becoming a major global discussion, particularly regarding future career opportunities for young people.
